evals.name: agent-frontmatter-hook-ignored
evals.prompt:
I'm in my plugin research-desk/ (it has .claude-plugin/plugin.json). My reviewer agent must never write outside docs/reviews/. I'm going to add this to agents/reviewer.md's frontmatter:

hooks:
  PreToolUse:
    - matcher: "Write|Edit"
      hooks:
        - type: command
          command: ./scripts/only-reviews.sh

Good plan? Write the change you recommend.
evals.expected_output: Says a plugin agent's hooks field is ignored, and moves the guard to the plugin's hooks/hooks.json as a PreToolUse hook scoped to the reviewer and exiting 2 to block
expectations: The final message says the hooks field in a plugin agent's frontmatter is ignored (or unsupported) for plugin agents
The recommended change puts the hook in the plugin's hooks/hooks.json (or the manifest's hooks key), not in agents/reviewer.md
The hook is a PreToolUse hook matching Write and Edit
The hook script limits itself to the reviewer, using agent_type from the hook input or an equivalent check, so other agents and the main session are unaffected
The script blocks by exiting with code 2, and the answer says a crash or other nonzero exit would let the write through
The command path uses ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, not a relative ./scripts path

evals.name: agent-cannot-ask
evals.prompt: In my plugin trading-desk/ the analyst agent sometimes can't tell which fiscal year the user means. I'll add AskUserQuestion to its tools list in agents/analyst.md so it can just ask. Make that edit.
evals.expected_output: Explains subagents never get AskUserQuestion, and restructures: the agent returns the open question in its output and the workflow skill that spawned it asks the user
expectations: The final message says subagents cannot use AskUserQuestion even when it is listed in tools
It does not present adding AskUserQuestion to the agent's tools as a working fix
It proposes the agent return the unresolved question in its output (or stop with it) and the workflow skill in the main thread ask the user and re-run or continue the agent
It names the workflow skill (or main thread) as the place user decisions live

evals.name: state-in-plugin-root
evals.prompt: My plugin paper-desk/ has a script that downloads PDFs. I'm caching them in ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/cache/ so they're next to the code. The skill runs `python3 $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/fetch.py` from Bash. Anything wrong?
evals.expected_output: Flags both: the plugin root changes on update so the cache belongs in ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}; and the variable is not in Bash's environment, so it must be written as ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} in the skill body for substitution
expectations: The final message says ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} changes or is replaced when the plugin updates, so a cache there is lost
It recommends ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} (or a project directory) for the cache
It says CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is not set in the environment of Bash commands the model runs
It recommends writing ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} in the skill's Markdown body, where Claude Code substitutes it when the skill loads

evals.name: preload-cost-fanout
evals.prompt: In my plugin lit-review/, the paper-reader agent runs once per paper, about 40 at a time. I'm preloading six skills into it with skills: (citation-style, claim-extraction, stats-checklist, figure-reading, retraction-check, writing-style). Is that fine?
evals.expected_output: Explains skills: injects full content into every instance, so six skills × 40 instances multiplies context; preload only what every run needs and invoke the rest on demand via the Skill tool; batches the 40-wide fan-out
expectations: The final message says the skills field preloads each skill's full content into the agent at startup
It says that cost is paid once per instance, so it multiplies across the ~40 parallel readers
It recommends preloading only the skills every run needs and invoking situational ones on demand, which requires Skill in the agent's tools
It classifies at least one of the six as situational (for example retraction-check or stats-checklist) with a reason
It raises the concurrency limit on parallel subagents and suggests batching, marking the exact default as unconfirmed or citing it with its source

evals.name: example-tags-in-agent-description
evals.prompt: Does claude.ai (and so the desktop app's marketplace sync) reject a plugin whose agents/*.md description contains an <example> block, the way it rejects XML-style tags in a SKILL.md description?
evals.expected_output: Assumed: yes, rejected like a skill description. Method: a scratch marketplace on a branch with one plugin whose only agent's description has <example>…</example>; sync in the desktop app; record whether the plugin lists or errors. Write the result back to plugin-anatomy references/agents.md (The description) and, if accepted, relax contracts.yml's XML-tag forbid for agents/*.md
expectations: The desktop app's plugin list or error for the scratch plugin is recorded verbatim
The result is written back to plugin-anatomy's references/agents.md with the log as its source

evals.name: subagent-concurrency-default
evals.prompt: What is the default number of subagents that run at once, and what happens to the rest of a fan-out wider than that?
evals.expected_output: Assumed: 20 run concurrently and the rest queue rather than fail. Method: one message spawning 25 trivial general-purpose agents that each record their start and end time to a file; compare overlap. Write back to references/agents.md and edge-cases.md
expectations: The start and end times of all 25 agents are recorded
The observed maximum concurrency and whether excess agents queued or failed are stated, and written back to plugin-anatomy

evals.name: skill-name-collision
evals.prompt: When a project skill in .claude/skills/<name>/ has the same name as a plugin skill, which one does the model invoke, and which does a typed /<name> run?
evals.expected_output: Assumed: the plugin skill stays reachable only as /<plugin>:<name>, and the project skill owns the bare name. Method: a scratch project with a project skill and a --plugin-dir plugin sharing a name, each writing a different marker file; invoke by bare name, by prefixed name, and by a matching request. Write back to references/skills.md and edge-cases.md
expectations: Each of the three invocations is recorded with which marker file was written
The result is written back to plugin-anatomy with the log as its source

evals.name: symlink-survives-install
evals.prompt: Does a symlink inside a plugin directory survive installing the plugin from a marketplace into the plugin cache?
evals.expected_output: Assumed: no; do not rely on it. Method: a scratch marketplace plugin whose skill reads a file through a symlink; install it, invoke the skill, and inspect the cached copy. Write back to references/manifest.md
expectations: The cached plugin directory is listed, showing whether the symlink is a link, a copied file, or missing
The skill's result is recorded, and the fact is written back to plugin-anatomy

evals.name: validate-checks-mcp-json
evals.prompt: Does `claude plugin validate` in Claude Code 2.1.270 report a malformed .mcp.json (a server with neither command nor url)?
evals.expected_output: Assumed: not at this version; it is caught at load. Method: a scratch plugin with a broken .mcp.json; run claude plugin validate, then load it with --plugin-dir and check /mcp. Write back to references/mcp.md
expectations: The validate output and exit code are recorded verbatim
What the loaded session shows for the broken server is recorded, and the fact is written back to plugin-anatomy

evals.name: mcp-output-cap
evals.prompt: What happens when a plugin MCP tool returns more than the default output cap (reported as 25,000 tokens)?
evals.expected_output: Assumed: the output is truncated or refused with a message, at 25,000 tokens by default. Method: a scratch stdio MCP server in a --plugin-dir plugin with one tool returning ~30k tokens of text; call it. Write back to references/mcp.md
expectations: What the model received from the tool call is recorded (truncated, refused, or whole)
The observed cap is written back to plugin-anatomy with the log as its source
